title: Tenant shielding: ingest flow control + trace handoff for on-prem collectors
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Background:
Redwood private and VPC deployments need stronger tenant-level ingress controls at the observability boundary to avoid noisy tenants taking down collector capacity, and to ensure trace continuity when we perform tenant isolation or replay. Current sidecar/collector behavior can lead to head-of-line latency and opaque trace gaps when ephemeral tenants exceed expected burst capacity.

Goal:
1) Implement a tenant shielding layer in on-prem/VPC collectors that enforces per-tenant ingest flow-control (burst, steady-state qps, backpressure policy) and graceful trace handoff semantics (preserve trace continuity, mark/annotate partial traces, and emit replay checkpoints).
2) Surface SLO-aligned latency/error dashboards and per-tenant health signals in the Console so platform teams can detect noisy tenants early and remediate.

Out of scope:
- Global multi-region routing changes (follow-up).
- Long-term archival replay pipeline (separate initiative).

Design summary and trade-offs:
- Flow-control model: token-bucket per-tenant with two burst tiers (soft, hard). Soft-tier throttles by delaying ack to the source (sidecar backpressure), hard-tier rejects with 429 + opaque tenant traceback when buffer saturation hits critical levels.
  Trade-off: token-bucket keeps steady throughput and is simple to reason about; however rare bursty ML workloads could see increased rejections — mitigated by a configurable burst window per tenant and temporary burst leases.

- Trace handoff: when a tenant's connection is paused or rejected, the collector will emit a trace-handoff span with metadata: tenant_id (hashed), handoff_reason, local_buffer_watermark, and an idempotency checkpoint token. Consumers (central relays / replay orchestrator) can use the checkpoint token to resume or reconstruct partial traces; traces missing spans are flagged for regression monitoring.
  Trade-off: adding handoff spans increases telemetry volume marginally but is necessary to preserve trace continuity and make missing-span detection deterministic. Handoff tokens are short-lived and rotated to avoid information leakage.

- Isolation boundaries: collectors will create per-tenant bounded queues and memory pools. When total collector memory pressure > threshold, eviction prefers tenants without burst-lease or with lowest SLA tier.
  Trade-off: this introduces complexity in allocator and eviction policy; we will instrument metrics heavily and keep the initial algorithm conservative (LRU-ish with SLA weight).

Acceptance criteria:
- Collector accepts per-tenant token-bucket config via CRD/console and enforces it under load for synthetic tenants (see test harness).
- When a tenant exceeds soft limit, source sidecar sees sustained increased request latency but no lost spans; when hard limit is reached, collector returns structured 429 and emits trace-handoff span.
- Console shows per-tenant ingest qps, head-of-line latency, buffer utilization, and count of trace-handoffs. Alerts firing for sustained head-of-line latency > 500ms and buffer utilization > 85%.
- Replay harness can resume a partial trace using the checkpoint token emitted in the handoff span and reconstruct trace parent-child relationships in 95% of test cases (synthetic trace replays).

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Schema & API: define handoff-span schema and checkpoint token format (short-lived opaque base64) — PR: github.com/redwood/collector/pull/3124 (WIP).
2) Collector runtime: per-tenant bounded queues + token-bucket enforcement; memory accounting hooks. Implement in C++ collector runtime with a Rust shim for the eviction policy so we can iterate safely.
3) Sidecar protocol: augment sidecar -> collector HTTP/gRPC with backpressure semantics and structured 429 bodies. Backwards-compatible: if old sidecar connects, collector will default to rejecting when hard limit triggers (graceful degradation).
4) Console: add tenant-level ingest panel, trace-handoff count, and dashboard alerts. Console-side will map hashed tenant ids to customer display names for authorized viewers only.
5) E2E tests: load generator harness with tenant mix, fault injection for network partitions, and replay/resume validation.
6) Rollout: start in internal Dedicated environment -> pilot select private customers with feature flag -> ramp to GA.

Testing & QA:
- Unit tests for token-bucket logic, eviction ordering, and handoff token lifecycle.
- Integration tests between sidecar and collector (simulate backpressure).
- Chaos test: inject sudden 5x traffic spike from one tenant and assert other tenants maintain latency SLOs.
- Replay test: intentionally drop a subset of spans and validate handoff-checkpoint resumes correctly.

Monitoring & Dashboards:
- New collector metrics (prometheus names): redwood_collector_tenant_queue_size, redwood_collector_tenant_tokens, redwood_collector_tenant_handoff_count, redwood_collector_heap_by_tenant_hash.
- Console dashboards: tenant ingest overview, tenant-heatmap for head-of-line latency, top-causers (by handoff count).
- Alerts: tenant_head_of_line_latency > 500ms for 2m (warning), > 2m (critical); collector_total_buffer_utilization > 90% (critical).

Rollout and migration notes:
- The new handoff-span schema must be backwards compatible with existing trace storage. We'll add a converter in the ingestion path to translate handoff spans into an internal annotation.
- For private/on-prem customers, the agent upgrade will be opt-in initially (feature flag). Ops playbook will include a rollback that clears per-tenant leases and drains buffers.

Risks and mitigations:
- Risk: Incorrect eviction policy could starve low-volume critical tenants. Mitigation: SLA-weighted eviction and safeguard to protect tenants with active canary tokens.
- Risk: Handoff tokens leak tenant identity if not carefully rotated. Mitigation: store only hashed tenant_id in emitted spans; token is opaque and bound to collector ID + TTL.
- Risk: Increased CPU/memory overhead on collector. Mitigation: benchmark targets and circuit-breaker to disable per-tenant queuing if host memory pressure is high.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- How long should handoff tokens be valid for replay (30s, 5m, 1h)? Proposal: 5 minutes to balance replay speed vs token surface area.
- SLA tiers mapping to eviction weight: need PM input on default weights and recommended burst windows.

Links & artifacts:
- Design doc (Confluence): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/INF/pages/847210/tenant-shielding-design (draft)
- Collector PR (WIP): https://github.com/redwood/collector/pull/3124
- Sidecar protocol sketch: https://docs.google.com/document/d/sidecar-backpressure-sketch
- Console dashboard mockups: https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/obs-tenant-shielding

Next steps this cycle:
- Finalize handoff-span schema and submit PR for API review (assigned to Marco).
- Implement basic token-bucket enforcement in collector runtime (ETA: +5 days).
- Build a minimal Console panel prototype to validate backend metrics ingestion (ETA: +7 days).

Handoff span emitted with opaque checkpoint token on hard-limit reject
Console shows per-tenant ingest and handoff metrics and alerts
Replay harness can reconstruct partial traces using checkpoint token in >=95% tests
